analysis: Both supplied units are head-text excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 421-1217). The PR only modifies documentation, and the changed ranges in the file_changes map (head lines 126-129, 3048-3049, 3100-3101, 4483+) fall outside the displayed excerpts. The excerpts are unchanged surrounding text and the changed hunks are in other units. The excerpts describe the Nemotron Super managed slot, the SSD prefix cache and GLM5Next serving. They state that checkpoints are encrypted under the provider's cache root, that coordinator text prefix reuse is partitioned by the authenticated cache scope and is off without one, and that image requests without a scope stay cold and never publish. Durable checkpoints are bound to the pinned shard SHA-256 and the prompt-contract hash. None of this contradicts T-041's described posture: HMAC-keyed lookup tags, authenticated per-account scope, TTL and the KEK purge. No code, trust-boundary or control change is visible here, and no threat assumption is invalidated. I did not see the patch hunks about the Gemma 4 pipeline lane default and the automatic policy widening, so I could not assess them. They are documentation of lane width, which affects availability and performance and not confidentiality. A later pass should check that the Gemma pipeline lane docs do not claim qualification or security properties the code does not provide. I found no actual regression.
